subject: Solutions to: Internal Error 457, Error 91 and Error about effort

messages.author: 5f6af0654b8b4648
messages.subject: Solutions to: Internal Error 457, Error 91 and Error about effort
parts:
Hello list



Thanks to the very patient Eric Rexstad, several errors and problems I had
with the MRDS and DSM engines were corrected. I have provided a summary
below in order to help anyone who has any of these issues in the future. As
a little background I was working with passive acoustic detections from a
line transect based survey (single observer).



Problem 1: Internal Error 457: "This key is already associated with an
element of this collection"

I managed to get abundance and density estimates which seem accurate easily
using CDS analysis without any errors. However when trying to the MRDS
engine it wouldn't run either half normal or hazard rate analysis due to
Internal Error 457.



Solution: The MDRS engine wants to work with double observer data, and even
though you can trick it into using single observer data the settings for the
survey type must be set to double observer and have a field 'Observer' which
would contain '1' for all detections.



Problem 2: **Error: The layer 'Line transect' specified by the Survey for
calculating efforts is higher than the sample layer specified in the Model
Definition.
Correct effort values can therefore not be calculated.**



Solution: Change the survey properties. Visit the Surveys Tab, Properties
button, Data fields tab and change the Effort Role to which ever layer
contains the Effort (for me the Segment layer).

If you look at the Dolphin.dst example, the effort is to be defined at the
segment (subsample1) layer of your project with a field found there. This
is different to the way in which "normal" distance sampling works wherein we
are interested in the lengths of various segments. With DSM, the modelling
is taking place at the level of the transect segments, so Distance needs to
know the size of the segments (defined using the field called 'Effort') that
contains the length of each segment.

Problem 3: Error 91: **Error Unexpected error** "Object variable or With
block variable not set". - in the DSM analysis



Solution: The problem was as simple as rerunning the detection function
fitting analyses after you had changed the Analysis preferences such that
the objects were not erased after their creation. I suspect you had run
analysis 1, then reset the preferences such that analysis 1 R results were
retained, then run your dsm analysis that complained that the analysis 1
results could not be found.



I hope this helps anyone having a simlar issues and thanks again to Eric
Rexstad from St Andrews University for his patientce and help with these
issues.



Anna



Anna Cucknell

Marine Conservation Research Ltd.
